text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning.

-A report from the European Council on xenophobia is criticising Norway for not fighting neo-Nazis, intolerance and racism hard enough. The report was released ahead of schedule at the request of news media and Amnesty International.

-The European Union will most probably refrain from imposing anti-dumping duties on Norwegian salmon imports. Only four countries support commissioner Sir Leon Brittan's proposal to impose a 14-percent tax on Norwegian salmon.

-Fokus Bank, which is the target of a hostile takeover attempt by a group of savings banks, says first-quarter after-tax profits rose by 56.5 percent to 182.5 million crowns partly because of higher interest income.
-Norwegian shipper John Fredriksen may register his shipping company Frontline in the United States.

-Several large commercial banks say they are not interested in taking over Fokus Bank. However the financial market still believes a rival bidder will exceed Sparebankgruppen's bid of 73 crowns per share.

-Defence Minister Joergen Kosmo, under pressure from the national audit office, wants to know if the United States has charged Norway too much for upgrading F-16 jet fighters in the Norwegian Air Force.
